name: Groom and triage new issues
description: Retired and kept disabled for its `authors` gate alone (ADR 0033). The Reconciler starts triage from `backlog-status.mjs --plan`, so this event would start the same issue a second time. The definition stays because `backlog-status.mjs` and afk-unblock read the trusted authors from the `authors` gates of the issue automations, and a repository whose automations gate nobody trusts nobody: without it the Reconciler would start nothing. Enabled, it ran issue-groom (om-auto-manage-issues, then afk-triage) on an issue a maintainer opened.

name: Re-triage when a hold is cleared
description: Retired and kept disabled for its `authors` gate alone, like the one above (ADR 0033). The Reconciler starts unblock and triage from `backlog-status.mjs --plan`, so this event would start the same issue a second time. Enabled, it ran issue-groom again when a person removed `blocked` from an issue.

name: Autopilot new pull requests
description: A PR opened as `rafalwolak` gets om-pr-autopilot, which diagnoses it and runs the right chain through to the squash-merge into develop (ADR 0031). There is one GitHub identity: every agent PR is authored by `rafalwolak` too, so the author filter only keeps dependabot and outside contributors out. Agent PRs are told apart by their pipeline labels instead: om-open-pr opens one carrying `review` inside its own chain (implement-ticket, issue-autofix), so `excludeLabels` stands down on `review` and every later pipeline label rather than race that chain. The standing develop-to-main promotion PR is opened with the owner's token too, and no filter here reads the base branch, so .github/workflows/promote-develop.yml opens it carrying `do-not-merge`, which is excluded: an unattended run never touches the release (ADR 0032).

name: Merge reviewed agent pull requests
description: A PR that om-auto-review-pr approved into `merge-queue` gets om-pr-autopilot --allow-merge, which squash-merges it into develop through om-approve-merge-pr (ADR 0031). A backstop for the implement chain, which drives its own PR to the merge: a reviewed PR whose chain ended early is picked up here. `authors` stays `rafalwolak`: every agent PR is authored by that one account, and the filter keeps dependabot and outsider PRs out of the unattended merge (the pinned stack, AGENTS.md). The develop-to-main promotion PR carries `do-not-merge` and never `merge-queue`, so it never matches (ADR 0032).

name: Weekly architecture review
description: Mondays: afk-architecture-review reads the last 30 days of hot spots and files at most three refactor issues, each with a recommendation strength. Read-only on code - the only writes are issues, which the Reconciler then triages and briefs like any other (ADR 0033); a security defect it finds is filed outside the three-issue cap. It reads `.ai/skills/afk-codebase-design/SKILL.md` for its vocabulary, and this repository's own seams are in the override beside it.

task.prompt: Run the afk-architecture-review skill for {{project}} on {{date}}.

name: Weekly lessons
description: Fridays: afk-lessons turns mistakes repeated across the last 14 days of pull requests into enforced rules - mechanical ones into a lint rule, judgement into CODE_REVIEW.md, operational into AGENTS.md. A lesson seen only once is not a rule, so a quiet fortnight is a no-op, and it opens at most one pull request per run.

task.prompt: Run the afk-lessons skill for {{project}} on {{date}}.
